nodes.summary: For natural numbers $s$, $t$ and $N$, the classical Ramsey property for $(s, t)$ holds at $N$ when every simple graph $G$ on $N$ vertices contains the complete graph $K_s$ as a subgraph, or its complement $\overline{G}$ contains $K_t$ as a subgraph.
nodes.title: The Ramsey property for cliques

nodes.summary: The proposition asserts that there is a real number $C > 0$ such that for every natural number $n$ and every simple graph $G$ on $n$ vertices in which no two adjacent vertices both have degree at least $3$, the diagonal Ramsey number $R(G, G)$ is at most $Cn$.
nodes.title: Erdős Problem 800 on linear Ramsey numbers

nodes.summary: There is a real number $C > 0$ such that for every natural number $n$ and every simple graph $G$ on $n$ vertices in which no two adjacent vertices both have degree at least $3$, the diagonal Ramsey number $R(G, G)$ is at most $Cn$.
nodes.title: Alon's theorem on linear Ramsey numbers

nodes.summary: For every natural number $k \ge 3$ there is an $M$ such that for every $m \ge M$ and every finite simple graph $H$ with exactly $m$ edges and no isolated vertices, the Ramsey number $R(C_k, H)$ of the cycle $C_k$ on $k$ vertices and $H$ is at most $2m + \lfloor (k-1)/2 \rfloor$.
nodes.title: Resolution of Erdős Problem 570

nodes.summary: The statement that for every natural number $k \ge 3$ there is an $M$ such that for every $m \ge M$ and every finite simple graph $H$ with exactly $m$ edges and no isolated vertices, the Ramsey number $R(C_k, H)$ of the cycle $C_k$ on $k$ vertices and $H$ is at most $2m + \lfloor (k-1)/2 \rfloor$.
nodes.title: Erdős Problem 570 (cycle versus graph Ramsey bound)

nodes.summary: For a finite simple graph $G$, the diagonal Ramsey number of $G$ is $R(G, G)$: the least $n$ such that for every simple graph $C$ on $n$ vertices, $C$ or its complement contains a copy of $G$ as a subgraph, and $0$ if there is no such $n$.
nodes.title: Diagonal Ramsey number of a graph

nodes.summary: For finite simple graphs $G$ and $H$, the Ramsey number $R(G, H)$ equals the infimum in $\mathbb{N}$ (where the empty set has infimum $0$) of the set of $n$ such that every simple graph $C$ on $n$ vertices contains a copy of $G$ as a subgraph or has a complement containing a copy of $H$ as a subgraph.
nodes.title: The pair Ramsey number as an infimum

nodes.summary: For finite simple graphs $G$ and $H$, the Ramsey number $R(G, H)$ is the least $n$ such that every simple graph $C$ on $n$ vertices contains a copy of $G$ as a subgraph or has a complement containing a copy of $H$ as a subgraph, and $0$ if there is no such $n$.
nodes.title: Ramsey number of a pair of graphs

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $s$ and $t$, the Ramsey number $R(s, t)$ equals the infimum in $\mathbb{N}$ (where the empty set has infimum $0$) of the set of $N$ such that every simple graph on $N$ vertices contains the complete graph $K_s$ as a subgraph or has a complement containing $K_t$ as a subgraph.
nodes.title: Classical Ramsey numbers as an infimum

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $s$ and $t$, the Ramsey number $R(s, t)$ is the least $N$ such that every simple graph on $N$ vertices contains the complete graph $K_s$ as a subgraph or has a complement containing $K_t$ as a subgraph, and $0$ if there is no such $N$.

Here $R(K_3, G)$ is the Ramsey number of the pair: the least $N$ such that every graph on $N$ vertices contains a triangle or has a complement containing a copy of $G$.

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
